title: A release's own body claims a PR that never actually merged
author: off-by-one
description: Extracts every claim phrase (ships/includes/merges/via #N) from a GitHub release's own body text and checks the named pull request's real state. A PR that exists but is not merged (still open, or closed without merging) is the seam: the release is a permanent public record that says something shipped which, in fact, did not.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the release published, mirroring merged-pr-issue-still-open's own reasoning: a claim checked within a few hours of publish might still be a race against a merge/release ordering hiccup rather than a genuine documentation error (0.5, below the 0.70 bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden); a full day or more past publish with the named PR still unmerged is unambiguous (flat 0.85, no further keyword fuzziness to misfire on -- the release body text is static once published). A named PR that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 -- that broken reference is dangling-issue-reference's own seam, not this one's. A named PR that IS merged is excluded at confidence 0.0 too, named not hidden, the same as scan.py's excluded list -- the claim was true.
